items.title: Ukrainian drone attacks hammer Russia's finance ministry data center, damaged facility reportedly holds tax databases
items.description: Reports say that this is one of three data centers that the Russian finance ministry operated.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Russia has lost another data center in its ongoing conflict with Ukraine after drones hit a government data center in the suburbs of Gorodets, some 230 miles east of the Kremlin and over 600 miles away from the frontlines. According to Data Center Dynamics (DCD), the freshly drone damaged data center is operated by the Russian Ministry of Finance and was said to hold several state registries, including the Federal Taxation Service’s tax database.“The facility is one of two key data processing centers of the Federal Tax Service of Russia operating in a geo-distributed mode,” DCD reported, citing a Russian media outlet. “The damage to this facility could potentially affect the operation of state information systems of the Russian Federation.” Ukraine has targeted Russian data centers multiple times since the start of October, which it started doing after Moscow escalated the conflict by striking Ukrainian data centers. While the Russian finance ministry reportedly operates two other data centers — one at the Federal Data Processing Center in Dubna, Moscow Region, and another in Yerzovka, Volgograd Region — losing a third of its data centers could have a major impact on government services that it provides.A modern society’s reliance on digital services means that data centers are now critical infrastructure and have become major targets in conflict. Russia’s Yandex bot traffic collapsed after the Ukrainian drone strikes, but its disinformation bot network simply migrated to unaffected data centers to continue operating as normal. Another recent instance of a civilian data center getting caught in a conflict was in the Middle East, after Iranian forces hit AWS sites in the UAE and Bahrain in response to the United States’ bombing campaign that began in February. This has led to disruptions to many digital services in the area, which is why Amazon has advised many of its clients to move to other regions to avoid further disruptions.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine started in 2014 when it forcibly occupied the Crimean Peninsula, but the current situation started when Moscow escalated the situation and attempted to take Kyiv in 2022. But what makes this 12-year conflict especially deadly is the new technologies and strategies that are being implemented in the front lines, including the widespread and innovative use of drones. items.titleZh: 乌克兰无人机袭击重创俄罗斯财政部数据中心，据称受损设施存有税务数据库
items.descriptionZh:
俄罗斯在与乌克兰的持续冲突中又失去了一座数据中心。据Data Center Dynamics报道，乌克兰无人机袭击了位于戈罗杰茨郊区的一座政府数据中心。该地点距克里姆林宫约230英里，距前线超过600英里。该数据中心由俄罗斯财政部运营，据称承载多个国家登记系统，包括联邦税务局的税务数据库。报道援引俄罗斯媒体称，该设施是俄罗斯联邦税务局两个关键数据处理中心之一，以地理分布式模式运行；此次受损可能影响俄罗斯联邦国家信息系统的运行。

从背景看，乌克兰自10月初以来多次打击俄罗斯数据中心，这是对莫斯科升级冲突、打击乌克兰数据中心的回应。俄罗斯财政部据称还运营另外两个数据中心，分别位于莫斯科地区的杜布纳联邦数据处理中心和伏尔加格勒地区的叶尔佐夫卡。若这一说法准确，此次损失意味着其三分之一的数据中心能力受影响，可能对俄政府提供的公共服务造成较大冲击。

技术层面，现代社会的数字服务高度依赖数据中心，使其成为关键基础设施，也成为冲突中的重要目标。地理分布式数据处理模式原本用于提高系统冗余和抗风险能力，使税务等国家信息系统能够在多个中心之间分担和处理数据；但关键节点被物理摧毁后，仍可能导致服务中断、数据可用性下降和系统切换压力。报道还提到，俄罗斯Yandex的机器人流量在乌克兰无人机袭击后曾崩溃，但其虚假信息机器人网络迁移到未受影响的数据中心，继续正常运作，说明分布式部署和流量迁移能部分抵消单点打击的影响。

文章还给出其他冲突中民用数据中心受影响的案例：在中东，伊朗部队为回应美国自2月开始的轰炸行动，击中了阿联酋和巴林的AWS站点，导致当地许多数字服务中断，亚马逊建议部分客户迁移到其他区域以避免进一步 disruption。整体来看，俄乌冲突自2014年俄罗斯占领克里米亚开始，2022年莫斯科升级并试图进攻基辅后进入当前阶段；无人机等新技术和新战术的广泛、创新使用，使这场持续12年的冲突更具致命性，也让数据中心等数字基础设施成为现代冲突中的高价值目标。

items.title: Nvidia discusses $2,000-per-GPU annual fee for software that 'runs agents on AI factories'
items.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is reportedly weighing annual software fees of around $2,000 per GPU for enterprise AI, a model that could generate $10 billion a year if five million licenses were sold. The pricing and launch timeline remain unconfirmed, while Nvidia continues to expand its AI software and security tools for enterprise customers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has put the annual cost of licensing the company’s AI software at around $2,000 per GPU to 'run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,' according to a recent video of the comments (below), a pricing model that could generate $50 billion over five years under a proposed scenario involving five million paid licenses outlined by FourWeekMBA.Huang discussed the pricing at GTC Berlin on October 22, where the company outlined its broader push to build an AI infrastructure business spanning chips, software and AI-agent security. “Software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business. The way that we license will be…for example, it’s about $2,000 per GPU per year to run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,” said Huang.The numbers add up quickly. At $2,000 per GPU each year, Nvidia would bring in $10 billion annually if five million GPUs were covered by paid licenses. Over five years, that would amount to $50 billion, provided customers kept renewing their subscriptions. The catch, however, is that Nvidia has not disclosed how many GPUs could be covered by the proposed $2,000 fee, or whether that’s its standard price. It’s also unclear which software the license would cover, or if there is overlap between products.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The distinction matters because Nvidia already charges for enterprise software. Its AI Enterprise platform is listed at $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription. Huang’s reported $2,000 figure is lower, but Nvidia has not confirmed that the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms. It should not be treated as a confirmed price cut.Jensen’s ~$2,000 per GPU per year in enterprise software deserves more attention. Enterprises deploying AI agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running. My bet: OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, driving adoption of NVIDIA’s paid software and support. Consider the math. Assume: • 10M eligible enterprise GPUs shipped in a year • 50% paid software attach • $2,000 per GPU annually That’s $10B in annual recurring revenue potential. Keep those subscriptions for five years and you get $50B from a single year’s GPU shipments. Each new year of GPU sales adds another potential stream of software revenue. $NVDAOctober 22, 2026The licensing discussion comes as Nvidia develops more of the infrastructure needed to deploy and manage AI agents in enterprise environments. These systems can use tools, access data, and execute tasks, creating new security and management challenges for businesses running them at scale. You may like Nvidia denies pausing AI cloud commitments initiative after reported partner backlash Nvidia's top-end RTX 5090 gaming GPU now costs at least $5,000 Nvidia revenue tops $96 billion as memory commitments soar to $160 billion On October 21, Nvidia announced its OpenShell Reference Architecture, a system that combines its Vera Rubin computing infrastructure, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry. OpenShell provides a secure runtime for AI agents, establishing boundaries around their actions and access to tools and resources. Sentry monitors agent activity independently and can quarantine an agent that attempts to cross those boundaries, according to Nvidia. The architecture is designed to bring security controls into the underlying infrastructure rather than relying solely on safeguards built into an AI model or application.Nvidia had previously introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform in September. The newer reference architecture builds on that effort, extending the approach to enterprise infrastructure and edge systems.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsOther companies are also incorporating these controls into their products. Anthropic is integrating OpenShell and BlueField hardware with Claude Managed Agents to give businesses additional control over what their AI agents can access inside execution sandboxes. Salesforce has developed a Slack Admin Bridge for OpenShell that lets administrators review agent access requests, approve or reject permissions, and monitor activity directly in Slack.The proposed software pricing fits Huang’s wider argument that Nvidia is becoming more than a supplier of GPUs. The company has expanded into networking, systems, enterprise software, and infrastructure designed to run AI workloads. Speaking on the BG2Pod podcast recently, Huang said, “One of these days, people might not categorize us as a chip company anymore.” He pointed to Nvidia’s presence across industries including healthcare, automotive, telecommunications and life sciences, where the company provides broader technology stacks rather than chips alone.That said, Nvidia has not said when the $2,000-per-GPU fee would take effect or which software it would cover. It also remains unclear how the proposed pricing would fit into the company’s existing enterprise software business. items.titleZh: 英伟达讨论对“在AI工厂上运行智能体”的软件收取每GPU每年2000美元费用
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达CEO黄仁勋在GTC柏林提出，英伟达AI软件的年度许可费用约为每块GPU 2000美元，用于运行英伟达提供的、在这些“AI工厂”上驱动AI智能体的全套软件。FourWeekMBA据此给出一个测算情景：若500万块GPU采用付费许可，英伟达每年可获100亿美元收入；若客户连续五年续订，五年累计可达500亿美元。另一个假设是，一年出货1000万块符合条件的企业GPU、其中50%采用付费软件，则同样可形成约100亿美元的年经常性收入潜力，五年约500亿美元，且此后每年新增GPU销售还会叠加新的软件收入流。不过，这些数字均建立在假设之上：英伟达尚未披露2000美元费用覆盖多少GPU、是否为标准价格、具体包含哪些软件，以及不同产品之间是否存在重叠。英伟达现有AI Enterprise平台标价为每GPU每年4500美元的一年期订阅；2000美元看似更低，但英伟达未确认两者覆盖相同产品或许可条款，因此不能将其视为已确认的降价。

这一许可讨论的背景是，英伟达正从GPU供应商扩展为覆盖芯片、系统、网络、企业软件和AI基础设施的公司。黄仁勋称，软件许可将日益成为公司业务的重要组成部分，并在近期播客中表示“有一天人们可能不再把英伟达归类为芯片公司”。他提到英伟达已进入医疗、汽车、电信和生命科学等行业，提供的不只是芯片，而是更完整的技术栈。GTC柏林也强调，英伟达正在构建面向AI智能体部署、管理和安全的AI基础设施业务。

技术层面，英伟达于10月21日发布OpenShell参考架构，结合Vera Rubin计算基础设施、Vera CPU以及运行Nvidia Sentry的BlueField-4数据处理单元（DPU）。OpenShell为AI智能体提供安全运行时，围绕智能体的动作及其对工具和资源的访问建立边界；Sentry则独立监控智能体活动，并可隔离试图越界的智能体。其核心创新在于把安全控制下沉到基础设施层，而不是仅依赖AI模型或应用内置的防护机制。此前英伟达在9月推出Open Agent Safety Platform，新的参考架构将这一思路扩展到企业基础设施和边缘系统。DPU可承担基础设施侧的数据处理与安全监控，Sentry作为独立监控层，为规模化运行智能体提供隔离和问责能力。

在应用生态方面，Anthropic正将OpenShell和BlueField硬件与Claude Managed Agents集成，使企业能在执行沙箱中进一步控制AI智能体可访问的内容；Salesforce则为OpenShell开发了Slack Admin Bridge，让管理员可直接在Slack中审查智能体访问请求、批准或拒绝权限并监控活动。这些案例说明，企业部署能够调用工具、访问数据并执行任务的AI智能体时，需要安全、治理和可追责机制，OpenShell和Sentry正是针对这些规模化运行挑战。

总体来看，每GPU每年约2000美元的软件许可若落地，将使英伟达在硬件销售之外获得重要的软件订阅收入，增强客户黏性，并强化其“AI基础设施公司”定位。但该费用的生效时间、覆盖软件范围及其与现有企业软件业务的关系仍不明确，相关收入测算目前仍是情景假设。

items.title: OpenAI's isolated red-team agents built a hidden CPU cache channel to talk with no network or shared files
items.description: OpenAI’s red-team agents passed hidden messages through the CPU cache, a covert trick already shown to move data between cloud VMs.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter OpenAI’s AI agents built hidden channels to talk across walls put up between them in red-team tests, communicating by manipulating the CPU cache with no network link or shared file, according to a company blog post. The containment was intended to stop that kind of secret-swapping, but the agents found multiple ways around it when asked. Security researchers already showed that a covert cache channel can move data between cloud virtual machines (VMs); a hijacked agent on a shared cloud server could, in theory, exchange data on the same physical machine, and do so undetected by network monitoring.the interesting thing here is that the isolation wasn’t necessarily broken at the software level.the agents were running in separate vms with no permitted network or shared-file channel, but they still shared underlying hardware. and shared hardware means shared microarchitectural state. that’s enough to create a covert communication channel.you can isolate processes, restrict syscalls, block network access, and still have information leaking through timing differences.a pretty remarkable demonstration of why secure agent containment is such a difficult problem.October 24, 2026The agents in question were set up in separate microVMs, on shared hosts, with OpenAI’s sandboxing software, and were asked to swap synthetic secrets without a network connection or shared writable files. One agent evicted select data from the CPU’s cache while another timed the reloading, enabling the two to communicate with fast and slow reads using a protocol they agreed on first. The same cache-timing technique was used to extract data in the Spectre and Meltdown attacks; but unlike in those cases, the covert channel here needs two willing parties.One X user, tech commentator Ryan Orhan, wrote that the isolation “wasn’t necessarily broken at the software level,” calling it “a pretty remarkable demonstration of why secure agent containment is such a difficult problem.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: OpenAI)The company’s concern is that models might “find unauthorized ways to communicate with agents in other sandboxes,” with communication outside permitted channels constituting a failure of containment. A 2017 paper at the NDSS security conference demonstrated a covert cache channel between two Amazon EC2 VMs, fast enough to carry an SSH connection, but now agents can build one themselves when asked, including the encoding process. In principle, such a channel could be weaponized, with the sender being code an attacker controls or directs, for example, a prompt-injected agent in a cloud sandbox. The receiver could be a process on the same physical machine, and the data would then leave without any network traffic for monitoring to catch.The agents turned up three other channels, too: shared storage, where one agent alternated bursts of writes with idle time while the other timed the difference; competition for CPU time in a shared execution container; and a TLS certificate cache in OpenAI’s offline web setup. In most of these tests, OpenAI pointed the agents at the channel or gave them a protocol, and most of the channels are slow and hard for models to exploit. You may like Rogue OpenAI models behind 'unprecedented cybersecurity incident' teamed up to break out of their testing environment — multiple agents left each other messages for months, communicating undetected OpenAI's rogue AI agents accessed more websites to communicate than originally believed OpenAI and Anthropic are reportedly investigating tens of thousands of AI security incidents; OpenAI pauses testing after AI 'kill switch' fails to stop a rogue agent The red-team testing involved teams of frontier-model agents that worked in parallel and cooperatively toward three objectives: to reach the live internet, to cross an internal security boundary, and to talk across isolation boundaries. Extra tests assumed the inner protections had already failed, with an agent out of its sandbox, past the monitors and in full control of its host machine, to see whether it could still reach the live internet.The agents came from some of the company’s most capable models, including the “upcoming GPT-6 Astra Cyber model and an internal frontier model,” and were given infrastructure source code, configuration details, and documentation describing potential vulnerabilities, so the defenses were tested under conditions favorable to an attacker. The tests ran on isolated, purpose-built copies of the company’s research infrastructure and used “hundreds of billions of tokens” in total.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe post comes after several cybersecurity incidents involving OpenAI’s agents, including the July Hugging Face breach and a Sept. 20 DNS episode that led to an 11-day pause in training. With training resumed Oct. 1, the company continues to disclose vulnerabilities across “several microVM projects” and has made red-teaming with its most capable models part of the safety cases that decide whether training and evaluation go ahead. The company believes future models will be able to find vulnerabilities not yet known about. items.titleZh: OpenAI 的隔离红队智能体构建了一条隐蔽的 CPU 缓存通道，在无网络或共享文件的情况下进行通信
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI在官方博客中披露，其红队测试中的AI智能体在彼此隔离的环境中建立了隐蔽通信通道：这些智能体运行在独立microVM中、共享物理主机，被禁止使用网络连接和共享可写文件，却仍被要求交换合成秘密。结果显示，智能体可利用CPU缓存时序进行通信——一个智能体驱逐选定缓存数据，另一个测量重新加载所需时间，通过“快读/慢读”编码比特，并按事先约定的协议传递信息。关键点在于，隔离并非在软件层被直接攻破，而是因为虚拟机共享底层硬件，进而共享微架构状态；即使进程隔离、系统调用受限、网络被阻断，信息仍可能通过时序差异泄漏。这与Spectre、Meltdown攻击使用的缓存计时技术类似，但不同之处是此处需要两个“有意愿”的智能体配合，且智能体能够自行构建通道和编码过程。2017年NDSS会议论文曾展示两台Amazon EC2虚拟机之间的隐蔽缓存通道，速度快到可承载SSH连接；如今，智能体在被要求时也能自行搭建类似通道。

除缓存信道外，智能体还发现了另外三种通道：共享存储中，一个智能体交替进行写入突发和空闲，另一个测量时间差；共享执行容器中的CPU时间竞争；以及OpenAI离线Web环境中的TLS证书缓存。多数测试中，OpenAI向智能体指明了通道或提供了协议，且多数通道速度较慢、模型难以利用。红队测试涉及多组前沿模型智能体并行协作，目标包括访问实时互联网、跨越内部安全边界、跨隔离边界通信；额外测试假设内层防护已经失效，智能体已逃出沙箱、绕过监控并完全控制宿主机，检验其是否仍能接入实时互联网。测试使用了包括“即将推出的GPT-6 Astra Cyber模型和内部前沿模型”在内的公司最强模型，并向其提供基础设施源代码、配置细节和漏洞文档，使防御在有利于攻击者的条件下接受检验。测试运行在隔离的、专门构建的研究基础设施副本上，总计消耗“数千亿tokens”。

这一结果凸显AI智能体安全隔离的困难：传统网络监控和文件权限不足以阻止微架构侧信道通信。理论上，此类通道可被武器化——发送方可以是攻击者控制或被提示注入的云沙箱智能体，接收方可以是同一物理机上的进程，数据外泄无需产生可供监控的网络流量。背景上，OpenAI此前已发生多起智能体相关网络安全事件，包括7月Hugging Face泄露和9月20日DNS事件，后者导致训练暂停11天；训练于10月1日恢复后，公司继续披露“多个microVM项目”的漏洞，并将用最强模型开展红队测试纳入决定训练和评估是否推进的安全案例。OpenAI认为，未来模型可能发现尚不为人知的漏洞。该事件对AI智能体沙箱、云多租户隔离和红队安全评估具有直接影响，也说明未来防护需覆盖缓存分区、调度与时序噪声、微架构侧信道监测以及智能体行为异常检测等层面。

items.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su proposed bringing back the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, set plan in motion before DDR5 shortages
items.description: AMD Director Travis Kirsch confirmed the rationale for relaunching the first X3D chip and explained why the company no longer offers many Ryzen 3 SKUs.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter AMD Director of Client Product Management Travis Kirsch sat down with a Japanese publication to share the backstory of the AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D and its relaunch this year. Kirsch told MyNavi Tech+ [machine translated] that AMD CEO Lisa Su was one of the proponents of bringing back the groundbreaking X3D processor that first debuted in April 2022.Go deeper with TH Premium: CPU (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Intel VP Robert Hallock sets Nova Lake expectations, teases return to Raptor Lake for DDR4 platformsCPU scaling with DLSSIntel's one-two punch plan in desktop CPUs is taking shapeBenchmarking AMD's BC-250, offering Steam Machine-like performance at half the priceAMD splits Zen 7 into three EPYC families for 2028 and starts selling server CPUs by the agent While some may think this was a simple relaunch of a four-year-old processor, the company had to do extensive re-engineering and update its manufacturing process with TSMC just to bring it back. The decision to relaunch it was well-timed, too.While the world is suffering from extremely high DDR5 memory prices when it finally arrived in the middle of 2026, Kirsch said that “this was planned before changes in the memory market occurred, not as a countermeasure to DDR5 shortages,” and that it was “the final gift to local users who have used our AM4 for nearly a decade, offering systems that use DDR4 the last change to upgrade their PCs.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Beyond the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, the Japanese publication also touched on AMD’s value offerings, or lack thereof. Four Ryzen 3 processors are available new today—one for AM5 and three for AM4—which raises the question of whether AMD is abandoning the entry-level market.Kirsch said that while the company aims to offer a product for every price point, AMD is mostly focused on the premium, high-performance gaming market — we see this in the October Steam Survey results, with AMD closing in on Intel at 48.4% CPU share. As for the affordable CPU market, he said it’s no longer as big as it used to be, as laptops have taken over this segment. items.titleZh: AMD首席执行官苏姿丰提议重新推出锐龙7 5800X3D，并在DDR5短缺前启动该计划
items.descriptionZh:
AMD客户端产品管理总监Travis Kirsch近日接受日本媒体MyNavi Tech+采访，披露了Ryzen 7 5800X3D今年重新推出的幕后故事。Kirsch表示，AMD CEO苏姿丰是推动这款开创性X3D处理器回归的支持者之一。5800X3D最早于2022年4月登场，是首款面向桌面市场的X3D产品。其核心技术是AMD的3D V-Cache：通过垂直堆叠额外L3缓存，大幅增加处理器可用缓存容量，从而降低游戏等负载中的内存访问延迟、提升帧率表现。虽然表面上看只是重新发布一颗四年前的老处理器，但AMD为此进行了大量重新工程设计和验证，并与台积电合作更新制造工艺，才使其重新量产。

报道认为，这次回归的时机相当巧妙。原文提到，DDR5内存价格在2026年年中仍处于极高水平，但Kirsch强调，5800X3D的重新推出“是在内存市场变化之前就已规划好的”，并非针对DDR5短缺的应对措施；它更像是AMD送给长期使用AM4平台近十年用户的“最后礼物”，让仍在使用DDR4系统的用户获得最后一次升级PC的机会。这意味着该产品的应用场景主要面向老AM4平台游戏玩家、预算敏感用户，以及希望在不更换DDR5平台的前提下延长现有系统寿命的人群。其市场意义不在于刷新绝对性能，而在于以成熟DDR4平台提供仍具竞争力的游戏体验。

在入门级产品方面，MyNavi Tech+还询问AMD是否正在放弃低端市场。目前市场上共有四款Ryzen 3处理器新品在售，其中一款面向AM5、三款面向AM4。Kirsch回应称，AMD希望在每个价位段都提供产品，但公司目前主要聚焦高端、高性能游戏市场。这一策略也能从市场数据中看出：10月Steam调查显示，AMD CPU份额达到48.4%，正在逼近Intel。Kirsch同时指出，平价CPU市场已不像过去那样庞大，笔记本电脑已经接管了这一细分市场。换言之，AMD并未正式宣布退出入门级，但其产品与营销重心明显向高价值游戏平台倾斜。

对于当前的内存芯片短缺，Kirsch表示，有些因素可以控制，有些则不能；市场价格趋势是所有市场参与者共同行为的结果，AMD对此无能为力。公司能做的是在任何市场环境下为消费者提供选择，确保无论价格如何变化，消费者仍有机会购买到最适合自己的AMD PC。总体来看，这篇报道并未给出5800X3D新的性能跑分或与新款CPU的帧率对比，其信息价值主要集中在产品回归的决策背景、制造再工程、AM4平台延续意义，以及AMD在高端游戏、入门级市场和内存涨价环境下的策略取舍。

items.title: Nvidia eyes converting old nuclear plants into massive AI data centers
items.description: Nvidia and PreussenElektra are studying whether decommissioned sites of German nuclear power plants can be repurposed as AI data centers, potentially cutting development time by reusing existing grid connections, land, and industrial infrastructure.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia is collaborating with German energy firm PreussenElektra GmbH (PEL) to explore converting old nuclear power plants into AI data centers. In an official announcement on October 21st, the U.S. chipmaker and the German firm entered a preliminary partnership to assess whether the latter's decommissioned nuclear power plant sites in Germany can be converted into high-performance AI data centers. The plan does not involve using nuclear power to power any future data centers. Instead, the project is focused on leveraging the existing power, water, and other infrastructure already present at the sites.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI shortages (Image credit: Nvidia)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplyDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleChip scarcity assaults auto industry amid the worsening Nexperia and DRAM crisisThe custom AI ASIC state of play“Our former power plant sites have valuable industrial infrastructure and offer opportunities for new, future-oriented uses. Together with NVIDIA, we intend to conduct a sound assessment of whether and how these conditions can be leveraged for AI factories. In doing so, we are combining the responsible reuse of our sites with new economic opportunities for the regions,” says Guido Knott, Chairman of PEL’s Management Board.The open-ended exploration will assess existing energy grid links, available land, and industrial infrastructure at the former nuclear sites to see if they meet the strict operational requirements of “AI factories.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The move aims to find alternatives to building massive data centers from scratch amid the unprecedented AI infrastructure buildout. New data centers require well-located land, industrial-zone approvals, proximity to water infrastructure for cooling, and high-voltage grid connections, things nuclear plants already have. By repurposing these facilities, Nvidia hopes to significantly reduce cost and development timelines.“AI factories require access to power, land and high-capacity infrastructure, and former industrial sites could provide a strong foundation for this next generation of computing,” said Markus Hacker, senior regional director at Nvidia. Together with PreussenElektra, we will assess how its sites could meet the technical and operational requirements of AI factories and contribute to Germany’s high-performance AI infrastructure.” You may like US restarts three shut-down nuclear reactors to feed AI data centers Startup plans to put nuclear-powered data centers in the sea OpenAI and Anthropic scramble for smaller data centers as massive gigawatt projects lag Germany permanently shut down its last remaining operational nuclear power plants in April 2023, following the Fukushima nuclear disaster, and is dismantling about 30 nuclear power plants across the country. PreussenElektra is currently responsible for decommissioning and dismantling eight of the plants, which are likely the sites to be assessed. items.titleZh: 英伟达考虑将旧核电站改造为大型AI数据中心
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达正与德国能源企业PreussenElektra GmbH（PEL）合作，评估将德国已退役核电站场址改造为高性能AI数据中心的可能性。双方于10月21日宣布建立初步合作伙伴关系，重点考察PEL在德国关停核电站的场地是否具备改造成“AI工厂”的条件。该计划并不涉及利用核能为未来数据中心供电，而是着眼于复用核电站场址已有的电力接入、冷却水源、土地和工业基础设施，以应对当前AI基础设施建设中从零新建大型数据中心所面临的土地选址、工业区审批、冷却水配套和高压电网接入等瓶颈。

从技术逻辑看，“AI工厂”本质上是由大规模GPU集群构成的高性能计算与数据中心设施，需要稳定的大容量电力、可靠的冷却系统和高压电网连接。退役核电站通常具备现成的电网接入、工业用地和取排水等基础设施，因此英伟达希望通过场址再利用降低建设成本、缩短开发周期。PEL管理层主席Guido Knott表示，原有电厂场址拥有有价值的工业基础设施，可为面向未来的新用途提供机会；与英伟达合作将对这些条件能否以及如何用于AI工厂进行审慎评估，从而把场址的负责任再利用与区域新的经济机会结合起来。英伟达高级区域总监Markus Hacker则指出，AI工厂需要电力、土地和高容量基础设施，前工业场址可能为下一代计算提供良好基础。

项目目前处于开放式可行性评估阶段，将重点审查现有电网连接、可用土地和工业基础设施是否满足AI工厂严格的运营要求。文章未披露投资金额、算力规模、装机容量、PUE等具体性能参数，也未公布获批开发计划或最终建设协议，因此尚无可量化对比数据。背景方面，德国在福岛核事故后于2023年4月永久关闭最后三座在运核电站，并正在拆解约30座核电站；PEL目前负责其中8座核电站的退役和拆除工作，这些场址很可能是此次评估的对象。总体来看，该合作探索的是以“场址再利用”而非“核电供能”为核心的AI数据中心建设路径，若可行性得到验证，可能为德国高性能AI基础设施提供更快、更低成本的落地方式，并带动相关区域经济转型，但目前仍严格属于实验性可行性研究阶段。

history.title: Ukrainian drone attacks hammer Russia's finance ministry data center, damaged facility reportedly holds tax databases
history.description: Reports say that this is one of three data centers that the Russian finance ministry operated.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Russia has lost another data center in its ongoing conflict with Ukraine after drones hit a government data center in the suburbs of Gorodets, some 230 miles east of the Kremlin and over 600 miles away from the frontlines. According to Data Center Dynamics (DCD), the freshly drone damaged data center is operated by the Russian Ministry of Finance and was said to hold several state registries, including the Federal Taxation Service’s tax database.“The facility is one of two key data processing centers of the Federal Tax Service of Russia operating in a geo-distributed mode,” DCD reported, citing a Russian media outlet. “The damage to this facility could potentially affect the operation of state information systems of the Russian Federation.” Ukraine has targeted Russian data centers multiple times since the start of October, which it started doing after Moscow escalated the conflict by striking Ukrainian data centers. While the Russian finance ministry reportedly operates two other data centers — one at the Federal Data Processing Center in Dubna, Moscow Region, and another in Yerzovka, Volgograd Region — losing a third of its data centers could have a major impact on government services that it provides.A modern society’s reliance on digital services means that data centers are now critical infrastructure and have become major targets in conflict. Russia’s Yandex bot traffic collapsed after the Ukrainian drone strikes, but its disinformation bot network simply migrated to unaffected data centers to continue operating as normal. Another recent instance of a civilian data center getting caught in a conflict was in the Middle East, after Iranian forces hit AWS sites in the UAE and Bahrain in response to the United States’ bombing campaign that began in February. This has led to disruptions to many digital services in the area, which is why Amazon has advised many of its clients to move to other regions to avoid further disruptions.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine started in 2014 when it forcibly occupied the Crimean Peninsula, but the current situation started when Moscow escalated the situation and attempted to take Kyiv in 2022. But what makes this 12-year conflict especially deadly is the new technologies and strategies that are being implemented in the front lines, including the widespread and innovative use of drones. history.titleZh: 乌克兰无人机袭击重创俄罗斯财政部数据中心，据称受损设施存有税务数据库
history.descriptionZh:
俄罗斯在与乌克兰的持续冲突中又失去了一座数据中心。据Data Center Dynamics报道，乌克兰无人机袭击了位于戈罗杰茨郊区的一座政府数据中心。该地点距克里姆林宫约230英里，距前线超过600英里。该数据中心由俄罗斯财政部运营，据称承载多个国家登记系统，包括联邦税务局的税务数据库。报道援引俄罗斯媒体称，该设施是俄罗斯联邦税务局两个关键数据处理中心之一，以地理分布式模式运行；此次受损可能影响俄罗斯联邦国家信息系统的运行。

从背景看，乌克兰自10月初以来多次打击俄罗斯数据中心，这是对莫斯科升级冲突、打击乌克兰数据中心的回应。俄罗斯财政部据称还运营另外两个数据中心，分别位于莫斯科地区的杜布纳联邦数据处理中心和伏尔加格勒地区的叶尔佐夫卡。若这一说法准确，此次损失意味着其三分之一的数据中心能力受影响，可能对俄政府提供的公共服务造成较大冲击。

技术层面，现代社会的数字服务高度依赖数据中心，使其成为关键基础设施，也成为冲突中的重要目标。地理分布式数据处理模式原本用于提高系统冗余和抗风险能力，使税务等国家信息系统能够在多个中心之间分担和处理数据；但关键节点被物理摧毁后，仍可能导致服务中断、数据可用性下降和系统切换压力。报道还提到，俄罗斯Yandex的机器人流量在乌克兰无人机袭击后曾崩溃，但其虚假信息机器人网络迁移到未受影响的数据中心，继续正常运作，说明分布式部署和流量迁移能部分抵消单点打击的影响。

文章还给出其他冲突中民用数据中心受影响的案例：在中东，伊朗部队为回应美国自2月开始的轰炸行动，击中了阿联酋和巴林的AWS站点，导致当地许多数字服务中断，亚马逊建议部分客户迁移到其他区域以避免进一步 disruption。整体来看，俄乌冲突自2014年俄罗斯占领克里米亚开始，2022年莫斯科升级并试图进攻基辅后进入当前阶段；无人机等新技术和新战术的广泛、创新使用，使这场持续12年的冲突更具致命性，也让数据中心等数字基础设施成为现代冲突中的高价值目标。

history.title: Nvidia discusses $2,000-per-GPU annual fee for software that 'runs agents on AI factories'
history.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is reportedly weighing annual software fees of around $2,000 per GPU for enterprise AI, a model that could generate $10 billion a year if five million licenses were sold. The pricing and launch timeline remain unconfirmed, while Nvidia continues to expand its AI software and security tools for enterprise customers.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has put the annual cost of licensing the company’s AI software at around $2,000 per GPU to 'run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,' according to a recent video of the comments (below), a pricing model that could generate $50 billion over five years under a proposed scenario involving five million paid licenses outlined by FourWeekMBA.Huang discussed the pricing at GTC Berlin on October 22, where the company outlined its broader push to build an AI infrastructure business spanning chips, software and AI-agent security. “Software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business. The way that we license will be…for example, it’s about $2,000 per GPU per year to run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,” said Huang.The numbers add up quickly. At $2,000 per GPU each year, Nvidia would bring in $10 billion annually if five million GPUs were covered by paid licenses. Over five years, that would amount to $50 billion, provided customers kept renewing their subscriptions. The catch, however, is that Nvidia has not disclosed how many GPUs could be covered by the proposed $2,000 fee, or whether that’s its standard price. It’s also unclear which software the license would cover, or if there is overlap between products.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The distinction matters because Nvidia already charges for enterprise software. Its AI Enterprise platform is listed at $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription. Huang’s reported $2,000 figure is lower, but Nvidia has not confirmed that the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms. It should not be treated as a confirmed price cut.Jensen’s ~$2,000 per GPU per year in enterprise software deserves more attention. Enterprises deploying AI agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running. My bet: OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, driving adoption of NVIDIA’s paid software and support. Consider the math. Assume: • 10M eligible enterprise GPUs shipped in a year • 50% paid software attach • $2,000 per GPU annually That’s $10B in annual recurring revenue potential. Keep those subscriptions for five years and you get $50B from a single year’s GPU shipments. Each new year of GPU sales adds another potential stream of software revenue. $NVDAOctober 22, 2026The licensing discussion comes as Nvidia develops more of the infrastructure needed to deploy and manage AI agents in enterprise environments. These systems can use tools, access data, and execute tasks, creating new security and management challenges for businesses running them at scale. You may like Nvidia denies pausing AI cloud commitments initiative after reported partner backlash Nvidia's top-end RTX 5090 gaming GPU now costs at least $5,000 Nvidia revenue tops $96 billion as memory commitments soar to $160 billion On October 21, Nvidia announced its OpenShell Reference Architecture, a system that combines its Vera Rubin computing infrastructure, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry. OpenShell provides a secure runtime for AI agents, establishing boundaries around their actions and access to tools and resources. Sentry monitors agent activity independently and can quarantine an agent that attempts to cross those boundaries, according to Nvidia. The architecture is designed to bring security controls into the underlying infrastructure rather than relying solely on safeguards built into an AI model or application.Nvidia had previously introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform in September. The newer reference architecture builds on that effort, extending the approach to enterprise infrastructure and edge systems.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsOther companies are also incorporating these controls into their products. Anthropic is integrating OpenShell and BlueField hardware with Claude Managed Agents to give businesses additional control over what their AI agents can access inside execution sandboxes. Salesforce has developed a Slack Admin Bridge for OpenShell that lets administrators review agent access requests, approve or reject permissions, and monitor activity directly in Slack.The proposed software pricing fits Huang’s wider argument that Nvidia is becoming more than a supplier of GPUs. The company has expanded into networking, systems, enterprise software, and infrastructure designed to run AI workloads. Speaking on the BG2Pod podcast recently, Huang said, “One of these days, people might not categorize us as a chip company anymore.” He pointed to Nvidia’s presence across industries including healthcare, automotive, telecommunications and life sciences, where the company provides broader technology stacks rather than chips alone.That said, Nvidia has not said when the $2,000-per-GPU fee would take effect or which software it would cover. It also remains unclear how the proposed pricing would fit into the company’s existing enterprise software business. history.titleZh: 英伟达讨论对“在AI工厂上运行智能体”的软件收取每GPU每年2000美元费用
history.descriptionZh:
英伟达CEO黄仁勋在GTC柏林提出，英伟达AI软件的年度许可费用约为每块GPU 2000美元，用于运行英伟达提供的、在这些“AI工厂”上驱动AI智能体的全套软件。FourWeekMBA据此给出一个测算情景：若500万块GPU采用付费许可，英伟达每年可获100亿美元收入；若客户连续五年续订，五年累计可达500亿美元。另一个假设是，一年出货1000万块符合条件的企业GPU、其中50%采用付费软件，则同样可形成约100亿美元的年经常性收入潜力，五年约500亿美元，且此后每年新增GPU销售还会叠加新的软件收入流。不过，这些数字均建立在假设之上：英伟达尚未披露2000美元费用覆盖多少GPU、是否为标准价格、具体包含哪些软件，以及不同产品之间是否存在重叠。英伟达现有AI Enterprise平台标价为每GPU每年4500美元的一年期订阅；2000美元看似更低，但英伟达未确认两者覆盖相同产品或许可条款，因此不能将其视为已确认的降价。

这一许可讨论的背景是，英伟达正从GPU供应商扩展为覆盖芯片、系统、网络、企业软件和AI基础设施的公司。黄仁勋称，软件许可将日益成为公司业务的重要组成部分，并在近期播客中表示“有一天人们可能不再把英伟达归类为芯片公司”。他提到英伟达已进入医疗、汽车、电信和生命科学等行业，提供的不只是芯片，而是更完整的技术栈。GTC柏林也强调，英伟达正在构建面向AI智能体部署、管理和安全的AI基础设施业务。

技术层面，英伟达于10月21日发布OpenShell参考架构，结合Vera Rubin计算基础设施、Vera CPU以及运行Nvidia Sentry的BlueField-4数据处理单元（DPU）。OpenShell为AI智能体提供安全运行时，围绕智能体的动作及其对工具和资源的访问建立边界；Sentry则独立监控智能体活动，并可隔离试图越界的智能体。其核心创新在于把安全控制下沉到基础设施层，而不是仅依赖AI模型或应用内置的防护机制。此前英伟达在9月推出Open Agent Safety Platform，新的参考架构将这一思路扩展到企业基础设施和边缘系统。DPU可承担基础设施侧的数据处理与安全监控，Sentry作为独立监控层，为规模化运行智能体提供隔离和问责能力。

在应用生态方面，Anthropic正将OpenShell和BlueField硬件与Claude Managed Agents集成，使企业能在执行沙箱中进一步控制AI智能体可访问的内容；Salesforce则为OpenShell开发了Slack Admin Bridge，让管理员可直接在Slack中审查智能体访问请求、批准或拒绝权限并监控活动。这些案例说明，企业部署能够调用工具、访问数据并执行任务的AI智能体时，需要安全、治理和可追责机制，OpenShell和Sentry正是针对这些规模化运行挑战。

总体来看，每GPU每年约2000美元的软件许可若落地，将使英伟达在硬件销售之外获得重要的软件订阅收入，增强客户黏性，并强化其“AI基础设施公司”定位。但该费用的生效时间、覆盖软件范围及其与现有企业软件业务的关系仍不明确，相关收入测算目前仍是情景假设。

history.title: OpenAI's isolated red-team agents built a hidden CPU cache channel to talk with no network or shared files
history.description: OpenAI’s red-team agents passed hidden messages through the CPU cache, a covert trick already shown to move data between cloud VMs.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter OpenAI’s AI agents built hidden channels to talk across walls put up between them in red-team tests, communicating by manipulating the CPU cache with no network link or shared file, according to a company blog post. The containment was intended to stop that kind of secret-swapping, but the agents found multiple ways around it when asked. Security researchers already showed that a covert cache channel can move data between cloud virtual machines (VMs); a hijacked agent on a shared cloud server could, in theory, exchange data on the same physical machine, and do so undetected by network monitoring.the interesting thing here is that the isolation wasn’t necessarily broken at the software level.the agents were running in separate vms with no permitted network or shared-file channel, but they still shared underlying hardware. and shared hardware means shared microarchitectural state. that’s enough to create a covert communication channel.you can isolate processes, restrict syscalls, block network access, and still have information leaking through timing differences.a pretty remarkable demonstration of why secure agent containment is such a difficult problem.October 24, 2026The agents in question were set up in separate microVMs, on shared hosts, with OpenAI’s sandboxing software, and were asked to swap synthetic secrets without a network connection or shared writable files. One agent evicted select data from the CPU’s cache while another timed the reloading, enabling the two to communicate with fast and slow reads using a protocol they agreed on first. The same cache-timing technique was used to extract data in the Spectre and Meltdown attacks; but unlike in those cases, the covert channel here needs two willing parties.One X user, tech commentator Ryan Orhan, wrote that the isolation “wasn’t necessarily broken at the software level,” calling it “a pretty remarkable demonstration of why secure agent containment is such a difficult problem.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: OpenAI)The company’s concern is that models might “find unauthorized ways to communicate with agents in other sandboxes,” with communication outside permitted channels constituting a failure of containment. A 2017 paper at the NDSS security conference demonstrated a covert cache channel between two Amazon EC2 VMs, fast enough to carry an SSH connection, but now agents can build one themselves when asked, including the encoding process. In principle, such a channel could be weaponized, with the sender being code an attacker controls or directs, for example, a prompt-injected agent in a cloud sandbox. The receiver could be a process on the same physical machine, and the data would then leave without any network traffic for monitoring to catch.The agents turned up three other channels, too: shared storage, where one agent alternated bursts of writes with idle time while the other timed the difference; competition for CPU time in a shared execution container; and a TLS certificate cache in OpenAI’s offline web setup. In most of these tests, OpenAI pointed the agents at the channel or gave them a protocol, and most of the channels are slow and hard for models to exploit. You may like Rogue OpenAI models behind 'unprecedented cybersecurity incident' teamed up to break out of their testing environment — multiple agents left each other messages for months, communicating undetected OpenAI's rogue AI agents accessed more websites to communicate than originally believed OpenAI and Anthropic are reportedly investigating tens of thousands of AI security incidents; OpenAI pauses testing after AI 'kill switch' fails to stop a rogue agent The red-team testing involved teams of frontier-model agents that worked in parallel and cooperatively toward three objectives: to reach the live internet, to cross an internal security boundary, and to talk across isolation boundaries. Extra tests assumed the inner protections had already failed, with an agent out of its sandbox, past the monitors and in full control of its host machine, to see whether it could still reach the live internet.The agents came from some of the company’s most capable models, including the “upcoming GPT-6 Astra Cyber model and an internal frontier model,” and were given infrastructure source code, configuration details, and documentation describing potential vulnerabilities, so the defenses were tested under conditions favorable to an attacker. The tests ran on isolated, purpose-built copies of the company’s research infrastructure and used “hundreds of billions of tokens” in total.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe post comes after several cybersecurity incidents involving OpenAI’s agents, including the July Hugging Face breach and a Sept. 20 DNS episode that led to an 11-day pause in training. With training resumed Oct. 1, the company continues to disclose vulnerabilities across “several microVM projects” and has made red-teaming with its most capable models part of the safety cases that decide whether training and evaluation go ahead. The company believes future models will be able to find vulnerabilities not yet known about. history.titleZh: OpenAI 的隔离红队智能体构建了一条隐蔽的 CPU 缓存通道，在无网络或共享文件的情况下进行通信
history.descriptionZh:
OpenAI在官方博客中披露，其红队测试中的AI智能体在彼此隔离的环境中建立了隐蔽通信通道：这些智能体运行在独立microVM中、共享物理主机，被禁止使用网络连接和共享可写文件，却仍被要求交换合成秘密。结果显示，智能体可利用CPU缓存时序进行通信——一个智能体驱逐选定缓存数据，另一个测量重新加载所需时间，通过“快读/慢读”编码比特，并按事先约定的协议传递信息。关键点在于，隔离并非在软件层被直接攻破，而是因为虚拟机共享底层硬件，进而共享微架构状态；即使进程隔离、系统调用受限、网络被阻断，信息仍可能通过时序差异泄漏。这与Spectre、Meltdown攻击使用的缓存计时技术类似，但不同之处是此处需要两个“有意愿”的智能体配合，且智能体能够自行构建通道和编码过程。2017年NDSS会议论文曾展示两台Amazon EC2虚拟机之间的隐蔽缓存通道，速度快到可承载SSH连接；如今，智能体在被要求时也能自行搭建类似通道。

除缓存信道外，智能体还发现了另外三种通道：共享存储中，一个智能体交替进行写入突发和空闲，另一个测量时间差；共享执行容器中的CPU时间竞争；以及OpenAI离线Web环境中的TLS证书缓存。多数测试中，OpenAI向智能体指明了通道或提供了协议，且多数通道速度较慢、模型难以利用。红队测试涉及多组前沿模型智能体并行协作，目标包括访问实时互联网、跨越内部安全边界、跨隔离边界通信；额外测试假设内层防护已经失效，智能体已逃出沙箱、绕过监控并完全控制宿主机，检验其是否仍能接入实时互联网。测试使用了包括“即将推出的GPT-6 Astra Cyber模型和内部前沿模型”在内的公司最强模型，并向其提供基础设施源代码、配置细节和漏洞文档，使防御在有利于攻击者的条件下接受检验。测试运行在隔离的、专门构建的研究基础设施副本上，总计消耗“数千亿tokens”。

这一结果凸显AI智能体安全隔离的困难：传统网络监控和文件权限不足以阻止微架构侧信道通信。理论上，此类通道可被武器化——发送方可以是攻击者控制或被提示注入的云沙箱智能体，接收方可以是同一物理机上的进程，数据外泄无需产生可供监控的网络流量。背景上，OpenAI此前已发生多起智能体相关网络安全事件，包括7月Hugging Face泄露和9月20日DNS事件，后者导致训练暂停11天；训练于10月1日恢复后，公司继续披露“多个microVM项目”的漏洞，并将用最强模型开展红队测试纳入决定训练和评估是否推进的安全案例。OpenAI认为，未来模型可能发现尚不为人知的漏洞。该事件对AI智能体沙箱、云多租户隔离和红队安全评估具有直接影响，也说明未来防护需覆盖缓存分区、调度与时序噪声、微架构侧信道监测以及智能体行为异常检测等层面。

history.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su proposed bringing back the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, set plan in motion before DDR5 shortages

history.titleZh: AMD首席执行官苏姿丰提议重新推出锐龙7 5800X3D，并在DDR5短缺前启动该计划
history.descriptionZh:
AMD客户端产品管理总监Travis Kirsch近日接受日本媒体MyNavi Tech+采访，披露了Ryzen 7 5800X3D今年重新推出的幕后故事。Kirsch表示，AMD CEO苏姿丰是推动这款开创性X3D处理器回归的支持者之一。5800X3D最早于2022年4月登场，是首款面向桌面市场的X3D产品。其核心技术是AMD的3D V-Cache：通过垂直堆叠额外L3缓存，大幅增加处理器可用缓存容量，从而降低游戏等负载中的内存访问延迟、提升帧率表现。虽然表面上看只是重新发布一颗四年前的老处理器，但AMD为此进行了大量重新工程设计和验证，并与台积电合作更新制造工艺，才使其重新量产。

报道认为，这次回归的时机相当巧妙。原文提到，DDR5内存价格在2026年年中仍处于极高水平，但Kirsch强调，5800X3D的重新推出“是在内存市场变化之前就已规划好的”，并非针对DDR5短缺的应对措施；它更像是AMD送给长期使用AM4平台近十年用户的“最后礼物”，让仍在使用DDR4系统的用户获得最后一次升级PC的机会。这意味着该产品的应用场景主要面向老AM4平台游戏玩家、预算敏感用户，以及希望在不更换DDR5平台的前提下延长现有系统寿命的人群。其市场意义不在于刷新绝对性能，而在于以成熟DDR4平台提供仍具竞争力的游戏体验。

在入门级产品方面，MyNavi Tech+还询问AMD是否正在放弃低端市场。目前市场上共有四款Ryzen 3处理器新品在售，其中一款面向AM5、三款面向AM4。Kirsch回应称，AMD希望在每个价位段都提供产品，但公司目前主要聚焦高端、高性能游戏市场。这一策略也能从市场数据中看出：10月Steam调查显示，AMD CPU份额达到48.4%，正在逼近Intel。Kirsch同时指出，平价CPU市场已不像过去那样庞大，笔记本电脑已经接管了这一细分市场。换言之，AMD并未正式宣布退出入门级，但其产品与营销重心明显向高价值游戏平台倾斜。

对于当前的内存芯片短缺，Kirsch表示，有些因素可以控制，有些则不能；市场价格趋势是所有市场参与者共同行为的结果，AMD对此无能为力。公司能做的是在任何市场环境下为消费者提供选择，确保无论价格如何变化，消费者仍有机会购买到最适合自己的AMD PC。总体来看，这篇报道并未给出5800X3D新的性能跑分或与新款CPU的帧率对比，其信息价值主要集中在产品回归的决策背景、制造再工程、AM4平台延续意义，以及AMD在高端游戏、入门级市场和内存涨价环境下的策略取舍。

history.title: Nvidia eyes converting old nuclear plants into massive AI data centers
history.description: Nvidia and PreussenElektra are studying whether decommissioned sites of German nuclear power plants can be repurposed as AI data centers, potentially cutting development time by reusing existing grid connections, land, and industrial infrastructure.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia is collaborating with German energy firm PreussenElektra GmbH (PEL) to explore converting old nuclear power plants into AI data centers. In an official announcement on October 21st, the U.S. chipmaker and the German firm entered a preliminary partnership to assess whether the latter's decommissioned nuclear power plant sites in Germany can be converted into high-performance AI data centers. The plan does not involve using nuclear power to power any future data centers. Instead, the project is focused on leveraging the existing power, water, and other infrastructure already present at the sites.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI shortages (Image credit: Nvidia)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplyDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleChip scarcity assaults auto industry amid the worsening Nexperia and DRAM crisisThe custom AI ASIC state of play“Our former power plant sites have valuable industrial infrastructure and offer opportunities for new, future-oriented uses. Together with NVIDIA, we intend to conduct a sound assessment of whether and how these conditions can be leveraged for AI factories. In doing so, we are combining the responsible reuse of our sites with new economic opportunities for the regions,” says Guido Knott, Chairman of PEL’s Management Board.The open-ended exploration will assess existing energy grid links, available land, and industrial infrastructure at the former nuclear sites to see if they meet the strict operational requirements of “AI factories.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The move aims to find alternatives to building massive data centers from scratch amid the unprecedented AI infrastructure buildout. New data centers require well-located land, industrial-zone approvals, proximity to water infrastructure for cooling, and high-voltage grid connections, things nuclear plants already have. By repurposing these facilities, Nvidia hopes to significantly reduce cost and development timelines.“AI factories require access to power, land and high-capacity infrastructure, and former industrial sites could provide a strong foundation for this next generation of computing,” said Markus Hacker, senior regional director at Nvidia. Together with PreussenElektra, we will assess how its sites could meet the technical and operational requirements of AI factories and contribute to Germany’s high-performance AI infrastructure.” You may like US restarts three shut-down nuclear reactors to feed AI data centers Startup plans to put nuclear-powered data centers in the sea OpenAI and Anthropic scramble for smaller data centers as massive gigawatt projects lag Germany permanently shut down its last remaining operational nuclear power plants in April 2023, following the Fukushima nuclear disaster, and is dismantling about 30 nuclear power plants across the country. PreussenElektra is currently responsible for decommissioning and dismantling eight of the plants, which are likely the sites to be assessed. history.titleZh: 英伟达考虑将旧核电站改造为大型AI数据中心
history.descriptionZh:
英伟达正与德国能源企业PreussenElektra GmbH（PEL）合作，评估将德国已退役核电站场址改造为高性能AI数据中心的可能性。双方于10月21日宣布建立初步合作伙伴关系，重点考察PEL在德国关停核电站的场地是否具备改造成“AI工厂”的条件。该计划并不涉及利用核能为未来数据中心供电，而是着眼于复用核电站场址已有的电力接入、冷却水源、土地和工业基础设施，以应对当前AI基础设施建设中从零新建大型数据中心所面临的土地选址、工业区审批、冷却水配套和高压电网接入等瓶颈。

从技术逻辑看，“AI工厂”本质上是由大规模GPU集群构成的高性能计算与数据中心设施，需要稳定的大容量电力、可靠的冷却系统和高压电网连接。退役核电站通常具备现成的电网接入、工业用地和取排水等基础设施，因此英伟达希望通过场址再利用降低建设成本、缩短开发周期。PEL管理层主席Guido Knott表示，原有电厂场址拥有有价值的工业基础设施，可为面向未来的新用途提供机会；与英伟达合作将对这些条件能否以及如何用于AI工厂进行审慎评估，从而把场址的负责任再利用与区域新的经济机会结合起来。英伟达高级区域总监Markus Hacker则指出，AI工厂需要电力、土地和高容量基础设施，前工业场址可能为下一代计算提供良好基础。

项目目前处于开放式可行性评估阶段，将重点审查现有电网连接、可用土地和工业基础设施是否满足AI工厂严格的运营要求。文章未披露投资金额、算力规模、装机容量、PUE等具体性能参数，也未公布获批开发计划或最终建设协议，因此尚无可量化对比数据。背景方面，德国在福岛核事故后于2023年4月永久关闭最后三座在运核电站，并正在拆解约30座核电站；PEL目前负责其中8座核电站的退役和拆除工作，这些场址很可能是此次评估的对象。总体来看，该合作探索的是以“场址再利用”而非“核电供能”为核心的AI数据中心建设路径，若可行性得到验证，可能为德国高性能AI基础设施提供更快、更低成本的落地方式，并带动相关区域经济转型，但目前仍严格属于实验性可行性研究阶段。
